ci.scope: Full supported-version matrix (11 smoke rows: torch 2.1 to 2.15, py3.10 to 3.13), lint, typing, packaging, nightly fast/mid/heavy/serial tiers and previews, weekly slow/rare and mutation margins, latest-torch canary, the opt-in 100k+ node graph suite, and the release dry run. Reuse an unchanged passing result; never rerun locally instead.
ci.status: Integrated 2026-10-03: every workflow runs on push to ci/** and on workflow_dispatch (release.yml on main only), and every job carries timeout-minutes within the budgets above (nightly jobs 30 to 120, weekly extended-tests 330).

notes: Inner loop: test-tier inner --changed PATH or --test tests/file.py::test_name. inner.map is generated by scripts/build_affected_test_map.py for every torchlens module (with reviewed coverage rows from scripts/affected_test_map_overrides.json); a changed path in inner.tier.paths (conftests, test plugins, pyproject.toml, import wiring, schema and contract modules, registries) runs the inner.tier marker tier instead. Other unmapped changes require reviewed targets and never fall back to the whole suite.

Commit gate: pytest tests/ -m smoke -n 4 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (pytest-xdist ships in the dev extra). Smoke is 395 coverage-chosen tests (tests/tiers/collection.json, collected 2026-11-06 in the pinned smoke environment; tools/tiers/collection.py regenerates it and --check compares it with a fresh collect-only output). Its estimated test time is about 1.5 minutes on 4 workers (the artifact's wall_estimate), plus about 40-45 s of collection per worker (under -m smoke the tiers plugin skips test modules off the smoke file list before import; measured 2026-11-02); tests/test_marker_lint.py caps it at 400, so a new smoke test needs a matching demotion.

Markers: smoke < 5 s each, heavy 5 to 20 s, slow > 20 s, serial runs without xdist (CI runs it in a separate step), rare is excluded by default, big_memory marks slow tests that exceed a 16 GB GitHub runner. Duration budgets are a repository check over tests/tiers/durations.csv (scripts/tier_durations.py check), not a runtime tripwire.

Pre_merge is the phase-boundary tier: 8 single-process shards over 'not rare and not slow' with one seed and one revision; --tier-shard (tests/_tiers_plugin.py) balances the selected tests by tests/tiers/durations.csv (each test capped at its file tier budget; a file heavier than a quarter of a shard is split test by test), the same split as python scripts/tier_durations.py shards --items. The tier measured ~21-26 minutes at -n 4 on a 4-core worker (~90 core-minutes), so ~12 minutes of tests per shard plus uv setup and collection, inside the 25-minute slice. Each shard is one process, so serial tests run safely. Timeout or a refused shard is incomplete validation, never a pass.

Weekly GitHub slow tier runs one pytest process per file (scripts/run_pytest_per_file_sharded.py), batching large files and running tests/test_real_world_models.py one test per process; big_memory tests are excluded there.

big_memory tests run in the project-registry scheduled suite weekly-big-memory (Sat 06:30 UTC on a large-memory fleet worker, 24 GiB, 2 h timeout), declared in ~/desk/provision/project-registry.json, not here.
tests/known_failures.py holds the strict-xfail ledger of known real-model failures (round 2); a fixed model turns its strict xfail red, so the ledger only shrinks.
Linux workers need uv, Python 3.11 and Graphviz. Oracle goldens exist per environment; off-canonical environments fail locally and skip only when CI is set.
